## Dataset: Herbivory mediates the response of below-ground food-webs to invasive grasses

Dataset supporting the paper &quot;Herbivory mediates the response of below-ground food-webs to invasive grasses&quot;, published in the Journal of Animal Ecology.  <br>The dataset refers to samples collected across 6 farms in the Bega Valley region of Australia. The farms are located in the grassy woodland ecoregion and are extensively managed with sheep and cattle grazing. Livestock shares the landscape with native mammalian and invertebrate herbivores. On each farm, two nested fenced exclosure systems were established. These included an open area, a fence excluding livestock but allowing access to native mammals and invertebrates, a fence excluding all mammals but allowing access to invertebrates and a shielded cage excluding all invertebrate herbivores as well. In each farm, one of these systems was located in a zone  dominated by the native Kangaroo grass, and another in a zone co-dominated by the Invasive African lovegrass. The sample and treatment numbering is provided in the file Sample&#95;metadata. <br>Soil samples were taken and DNA was extracted and amplified for 16s and ITS markers. The resulting metabarcoding derived ASV tables are presented &#40;16s&#95;ASV&#95;table and ITS&#95;ASV&#95;table&#41;, as are the inferred functional profiles for bacteria at the enzyme and pathway level &#40;16s&#95;picrust&#95;enzymes and 16s&#95;picrust&#95;pathways&#41;, as derived by the PICRUSt2 pipeline, and the fungal guilds reconstructed with FunGuildR &#40;FunguildR&#95;output&#41;. <br>Chemical, physical and enzymatic assays were also performed on the soil samples &#40;Chemical&#95;data&#41;.<br>Nematodes were extracted from soil cores with a Baermann funnel, counted &#40;Nematodes&#95;counts&#41; and had their DNA extracted and amplified &#40;Nematodes&#95;asv&#95;table&#41;. Soil invertebrates were sampled with below-ground pitfall traps and identified to family level &#40;Invertebrates&#41; and earthworms were manually extracted from 20&#42;20&#42;20 cm monoliths &#40;&#40;Earthworm&#95;counts&#41;. <br>Two 20 by 100 cm strips had their vegetation removed and their living and litter biomass quantified by dry weight &#40;Biomass&#95;summary&#41;. Sensors measuring moisture and temperature 10 cm beneath the soil surface were installed in each plot and their output is presented in Microclimate&#95;summary.

[View this dataset in the data catalogue](https://opendata.swiss/de/dataset/herbivory-mediates-the-response-of-below-ground-food-webs-to-invasive-grasses)

## Load packages

This template targets tidyverse (2.x) and skimr (2.x) with R 4.1 or newer for the native `|>` pipe; package versions are not pinned. Install missing packages once with `install.packages(c("tidyverse", "skimr"))`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

USER_AGENT <- "OpendataSwiss-StarterCode-R/1.0"
HTTP_TIMEOUT <- 30

get_dataset <- function(url, delim = NULL, drop_empty_unnamed = TRUE, ...) {
  if (grepl("^https?://", url)) {
    local_file <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(local_file), add = TRUE)
    old_options <- options(timeout = HTTP_TIMEOUT)
    on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
    status <- download.file(url, local_file, method = "libcurl", mode = "wb",
                            quiet = TRUE, headers = c("User-Agent" = USER_AGENT))
    if (status != 0) stop("Resource download failed")
    url <- local_file
  }
  data <- read_delim(url, delim = delim, show_col_types = FALSE, ...)
  stop_for_problems(data)
  if (drop_empty_unnamed && nrow(data) > 0) {
    # Blank CSV headers (often from trailing separators) become "...n".
    unnamed <- grepl("^\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", names(data))
    empty_unnamed <- unnamed & map_lgl(data, ~ all(is.na(.x)))
    if (any(empty_unnamed)) {
      message("Removed empty unnamed columns: ", paste(names(data)[empty_unnamed], collapse = ", "))
      data <- data[, !empty_unnamed, drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  data
}
```

## Load data

Selected resource: **65ea53ae-3a1b-4b90-b8df-5d6dff71727d** (CSV). This notebook loads only this resource.

For CSV, the delimiter and column types are guessed. Check the preview and metadata; set `delim`, `col_types`, `na`, or `locale` in `get_dataset(...)` when needed (for example, read identifiers with leading zeros as character columns). Parsing problems stop the import so they can be addressed.

Fully empty columns named `...n` are removed on import. Named empty columns and unnamed columns containing values are kept. Use `drop_empty_unnamed = FALSE` to retain every column, including intentionally named `...n` fields.

```{r load-data}
df <- get_dataset("https://www.envidat.ch/dataset/4bda5372-4c89-4db2-91c2-da8b2f55aacc/resource/a2d0a31a-cfb3-421c-9970-36f0f2ba9b5e/download/biomass_summary.csv")
```

## Missing values

```{r missing-values}
missing <- tibble(
  column = names(df),
  missing = map_int(df, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  missing_pct = map_dbl(df, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))
missing

# Show up to 20 columns with missing values; percentages use all rows.
missing_plot <- missing |> filter(missing > 0) |> slice_head(n = 20)
if (nrow(missing_plot) > 0) {
  ggplot(missing_plot, aes(x = missing_pct, y = reorder(column, missing_pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "Missing values (%)", y = NULL, title = "Missingness by column")
} else {
  message("No missing values to plot (or the dataset has no rows).")
}
```

## Summary and distributions

`skim()` reports completeness and type-specific summaries. Inspect units before interpreting numeric codes as measurements.

```{r summary}
if (nrow(df) > 0 && ncol(df) > 0) {
  skim(df)
} else {
  message("No data to summarize.")
}
```

```{r histograms}
# Plot up to four numeric columns, excluding non-finite values only from plots.
numeric_names <- names(select(df, where(is.numeric))) |> head(4)
for (column in numeric_names) {
  values <- df[[column]]
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  if (length(values) > 0) {
    plot <- ggplot(tibble(value = values), aes(x = value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
      labs(title = column, x = column, y = "Count")
    print(plot)
  }
}
```

```{r category-counts}
# Top 10 values for up to three categorical columns, including missing values.
categorical_names <- df |>
  select(where(~ is.character(.x) || is.factor(.x) || is.logical(.x))) |>
  names() |>
  head(3)
for (column in categorical_names) {
  cat(column, "\n")
  df |> count(.data[[column]], sort = TRUE) |> head(10) |> print()
}
```
